Broadcom Inc (AVGO US) Buy: Potent mix of ASIC and networking upside ◆ Significant FY26e AI revenue upside driven by ASIC momentum and networking TAM expansion ◆ Sizable upside to street estimates; our FY26e EPS relatively in line with consensus’ FY27e EPS ◆ Reinstate Broadcom (Buy) as our top AI semiconductor pick; TP +34% to USD535 and FY26-27e EPS +17-30%, both street highs ASIC momentum unstoppable even without OpenAI: We believe the street is still undervaluing the ASIC opportunity despite revising up FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue estimates by 47%/60% since 3QFY25 results. We believe AVGO has increased its FY26e CoWoS capacity allocation significantly from 150k wafers to 250k wafers. Alphabet (GOOGL US) continues to be the main driver for the incremental revision as we now expect Google tensor processing unit (TPU) shipments of 3.1m (from 1.7m) in FY26e. We now expect Meta ASIC shipments of 900k (from 750k) units driven by ramp of its Athena and Iris chips. We believe that the fourth customer announced is Anthropic and expect cUSD5bn ASIC revenue contribution in FY26e. Hence, we lift FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue +46%/+63% to USD44.7bn/USD72.0bn, now 44%/59% above Visible Alpha consensus of USD30.9bn/USD45.4bn. The OpenAI deal (10GW deployment) lacks clarity on the part Broadcom plays. However, if Broadcom does the full design of the chip, we estimate an ASIC revenue opportunity close to USD14bn per GW deployment with upside to networking revenue too. Networking can drive further upside driven by TAM expansion: The overall AI total addressable market (TAM) is expanding beyond traditional hyperscalers into emerging hyperscalers, enterprise and sovereign AI, driving the AI networking TAM higher too. Already the market leader in Ethernet switches, Broadcom has also matched digital signal processor (DSP) market leader Marvell’s roadmap with its 1.6T solution (see Marvell Technology (MRVL US): Initiate at Hold, 24 November 2025). Therefore, we believe AI networking could provide an earnings upside surprise. Hence, our FY26e/FY27e AI networking revenue estimates are 8%/11% above consensus. Our bull case scenario with FY26e AI networking revenue growth of 100% y-o-y (vs base case 50% y-o-y) implies further 4% upside to our base case EPS. Our FY26e EPS almost at par with consensus’ FY27e: ASIC strength and the networking upside opportunity can drive significant upside to consensus FY26e EPS estimates. We believe that the upside opportunity is so significant that consensus FY27e EPS can be achieved in FY26e. Our FY26e EPS of USD11.68 is just 5% below consensus FY27e EPS of USD12.31. Reiterate Buy; lift TP to USD535 (from USD400): Our USD535 TP is derived by applying a FY27 target PE of 32x (from 31x) to our FY27e EPS of USD16.72 (from USD12.85). With c51% implied upside, we retain a Buy rating on the stock. We believe the upside to ASIC and AI networking revenue can help AVGO re-rate towards its peak FY27e PE of 32x. Broadcom reinstated as our top AI semiconductor pick We reinstate Broadcom as our top AI semiconductor pick amongst our coverage driven by the following factors: We’re seeing strong demand from Alphabet for its TPU – now both for internal as well as external use. Meta is also expected to ramp its ASIC chips next year. As a result, we expect the CoWoS capacity for FY26e to expand from 150k wafer to 250k wafers driving our revised FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue estimates to be 44%/59% above consensus. ◆ We believe the overall AI TAM expansion beyond traditional hyperscalers will drive networking TAM higher as well. Hence, we believe the street is undervaluing AI networking revenue. Our FY26e/FY27e AI networking revenue estimates are 8%/11% higher than the street. ◆ The combined strength from ASIC and networking gives us conviction that Broadcom can deliver a significant upside surprise to street expectations. Hence, our FY26e/FY27e EPS estimates are the highest on the street – 24%/36% higher than consensus. ◆ Additionally, we believe that Broadcom can deliver consensus’ FY27e EPS estimates in FY26e as our FY26e EPS estimate of USD11.68 is just 5% below consensus FY27e EPS estimate of USD12.31. ◆ We expect Broadcom to have higher FY27e revenue growth of 35% vs the average of 27% for AI accelerator plays. We estimate Broadcom to grow earnings by 43% in FY27e vs the peer group average of 30%. Despite better growth expectations, it is trading at a 21x FY27e PE, virtually aligned with the peer group average of 20x. Hence, we believe the riskreward is very enticing.

ASIC momentum going from strength to strength In our 29 August note (Broadcom: No ST earnings surprise but remains our top pick, we had highlighted that the street was undervaluing the ASIC potential and had flagged the CoWoS capacity expansion as well as pricing premium. Our FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue estimates were 49%/59% higher. There has been significant consensus upward revision since then driven by the announcement of a fourth ASIC customer as well as the OpenAI deal. However, we believe the story remains the same— the ASIC potential remains significantly undervalued by the street. Recent developments have driven street estimates higher, but still not enough We’ve seen significant revision to ASIC revenue estimates since 3QFY25 financial results driven by ◆ the announcement of a new ASIC customer, Broadcom’s fourth, which would add an additional USD10bn in AI revenue in FY26e; ◆ and announcement of a deal with OpenAI on 13 October under which 10GW of systems that include accelerators and Ethernet solutions, co-designed by OpenAI and Broadcom would be deployed ◆ Since 3QFY25 results, the street has revised its FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue estimates by 47%/60% to USD30.9bn/USD45.4bn respectively. Primarily driven by this, the FY26e/FY27e EPS estimates have seen an upward revision of 13%/23%. Despite the significant upward estimate revisions highlighted above, we believe the street is still undervaluing the ASIC revenue opportunity for Broadcom. The street’s current ASIC revenue estimates for FY26e/FY27e of USD30.9bn/USD45.4bn are now in line with our old estimates of USD30.6bn/USD44.1bn.

TAM expansion continues amidst CSP capex upward revision trend
The hyperscalers capex growth momentum can be viewed as a proxy to ASIC growth as all hyperscalers have a current or future ASIC project at Broadcom or one of its peers. Since the beginning of the year, the consensus estimates for cloud service provider (CSP) capex for 2026e and 2027e have been revised up by 40% and 63%, respectively as the hyperscalers continue to expect aggressive investment in AI. While we continue to expect most of the AI spend out of CSP capex to go towards AI GPUs, we believe CSP capex expansion suggests TAM expansion for ASIC firms as well. We also still expect the spend on ASICs to keep increasing as we expect their contribution in total CSP capex to increase from 2% in 2023 to 13% in 2027e. Additionally, we estimate ASIC revenue growth at a CAGR of 119% through 2023-27e to outgrow AI GPU revenue which we expect to grow at a CAGR of 82% during the same period.

Core ASIC customers’ momentum driving significant capacity expansion
Alphabet remains one of the key ASIC customers for Broadcom as it ramps its TPU v6 with v7 expected to starting ramping next year. On 23 October, Alphabet announced that Anthropic will train and serve Claude models with plans to access up to 1m TPUs. So, we believe the extended demand for TPUs for external use cases in addition to Alphabet’s internal use will drive further unit shipments. As a result, we expect the CoWoS allocation for Alphabet TPU to increase to 130k wafers in FY26e from our previous estimate of c84k wafers. We also fine-tune our blended die and ASP estimates. We now expect Broadcom to ship 3.1m units of TPU (previous estimate of 1.7m units) and expect Alphabet TPU to contribute USD31.2bn in ASIC revenue in FY26e.
We also expect Meta to become a sizeable customer starting next year as it plans to ramp its two ASIC chips – Athena and Iris. Hence, we expect the CoWoS allocation for Meta to increase to 90k wafers in FY26e from our previous estimate of 50k wafers. We raise our FY26e unit shipment estimates for Meta from 750k to 900k and expect Meta to contribute USD7.2bn in ASIC revenue in FY26e.
In addition to ByteDance, which is expected to ramp its ASIC program next year, Broadcom also announced its fourth customer – which we believe to be Anthropic. For Anthropic, Broadcom announced that it has already received an order that could potentially add USD10bn to AI revenue. We expect the Anthropic order to be a rack-based solution. We believe the ASIC revenue contribution from Anthropic will be around USD5bn in FY26e.
Driven by the enhanced demand across its ASIC customers, we now expect a significant upward revision in Broadcom’s total CoWoS allocation for FY26e from 150k wafers to 250k wafers. We continue to expect latest-generation ASIC projects needing more computational power. Hence, moving to a larger die size in turn driving the ASP higher. We revise our FY26e/FY27e ASIC revenue estimates by 46%/63% to USD44.7bn/USD72bn. Our estimates are now the highest on the street – 44% higher than consensus’ FY26e ASIC revenue estimates and 59% higher than consensus’ FY27e ASIC revenue estimates.

CoWoS allocation continues to outpace GPU players Driven by stronger ASIC momentum from its core customers, we continue to expect Broadcom to have the highest CoWoS y-o-y capacity growth of 201% in 2026e. This is significantly higher than AI GPU companies Nvidia with 2026e CoWoS growth of 140% and AMD with 121%. OpenAI deal lacks clarity; we calculate USD14bn ASIC revenue opportunity per GW On 23 October, OpenAI and Broadcom announced a collaboration for 10 gigawatts of custom AI accelerators. OpenAI will design the accelerators and systems, which will be developed and deployed in partnership with Broadcom. The racks are scaled entirely with Ethernet and other connectivity solutions from Broadcom. Broadcom said it aims to start the deployment of the racks in 2H26, to complete by the end of 2029. From the press release, it remains unclear whether Broadcom is designing the chips or if the racks would be scaled using Broadcom Ethernet. While this deal can see a significant revenue contribution later down the line, we believe that the near-term momentum for its core customers is strong enough for Broadcom to surprise the street on the upside. We try to quantify the OpenAI deal revenue opportunity by assuming Broadcom does the design of the chips which are comparable with Alphabet’s latest-gen TP v6 i.e. Ironwood which has 9,216 chips in a pod as each pod consumes 10MW of power. We extrapolate the revenue opportunity by assuming the OpenAI chip will be comparable to Ironwood TPU. Based on our ASP assumption of USD15k per chip, we estimate that the revenue opportunity from the OpenAI deal could be USD14bn (rounded) per GW deployment. This is below some of the bullish market expectations of USD20-30bn per GW based on the recent GPU deals. Based on our estimate, the lifetime value of the deal could be USD140bn for ASIC revenue with further upside to networking revenue.

Increasingly bullish view on AI networking AI TAM expansion driving networking content growth The overall AI TAM is expanding beyond traditional hyperscalers into emerging hyperscalers, enterprise and sovereign AI, driving the AI networking TAM higher too. We estimate AI GPU revenue growth through 2023-27e at a CAGR of 82% and ASIC revenue growth at a CAGR of 119%. We believe this suggests increasing TAM for AI networking as more and more GPU sales implies more networking infra demand as well. Some of the recent ASIC deals are also more rack based which we believe will lead to higher networking content as well. AI networking upside driven by leadership in switches and DSP potential Broadcom continues to dominate the AI switch chip market, boasting a market share of around 70%. Broadcom’s Tomahawk 6 has a total bandwidth of 102.4 terabit per second (Tb/s) and can support 64 1.6T ports or 128 800G ports and is currently considered to be the most advanced solution available. Already the market leader in Ethernet switches, Broadcom has also matched DSP (digital signal processor) market leader Marvell’s roadmap with its 1.6T solution. While we continue to expect Marvell to retain its majority share in the DSP market, we expect Broadcom would be able to penetrate the market quicker than expected and gain sizeable share rapidly. Particularly for the 1.6T solution, we expect Broadcom to gain close to 40-45% market share by 2026e. With increasing networking content requirement driven by the AI TAM expansion beyond traditional hyperscalers, we believe AI networking could provide an earnings upside surprise. Hence, our FY26e/FY27e AI networking revenue estimates are 8%/11% above consensus. We expect AI networking revenue to grow by 50% y-o-y in FY26e compared to consensus estimates of 43% y-o-y growth. Sensitivity analysis on higher AI networking growth We conducted a sensitivity analysis based on AI networking TAM expansion driving higher than expected AI networking growth in FY26e. In our first bull case, we assume 75% y-o-y AI networking revenue growth in FY26e. This drives further implied upside of 2% to our base case EPS. In our most bullish case, we assume 100% y-o-y growth for AI networking revenue in FY26e. This drives further potential upside of 4% to our base case EPS. The implied EPS in our most bullish case is 27% higher than consensus estimates.

Broadcom can meet consensus’ FY27e EPS expectations in FY26e
The strong ASIC momentum coupled with upside to networking revenue can drive unprecedented AI revenue growth. Our FY26e AI revenue estimates of USD55.8bn imply 180% y-o-y growth and are 52% higher than consensus of USD36.7bn for FY26e. Our FY27e AI revenue estimates of USD88.2bn imply 58% y-o-y growth and are 64% higher than consensus of USD53.4bn.
According to our estimates, the contribution of AI revenue to overall revenue will continue to increase exponentially, increasing from 31% in FY25e to 64% in FY27e. Hence, our higher AI revenue estimates drive significant EPS growth as well. We believe that the upside opportunity is so huge that consensus’ FY27e EPS can be achieved in FY26e. Our FY26e EPS of USD11.68 is just 5% below consensus FY27e EPS of USD12.31.

Valuation inexpensive with strong growth on the horizon We expect the overall AI accelerator industry (both GPUs and ASIC players) to thrive in the coming years as hyperscalers continue to increase investment on AI as well as the overall AI TAM expanding beyond traditional hyperscalers into enterprise and sovereign AI. However, we see Broadcom as the company with the biggest growth prospects and we expect Broadcom to outgrow its peers. Driven by its sizeable ASIC revenue ramp starting as early as next year, we expect Broadcom to have higher FY27e revenue growth of 35% vs the average of 27% for AI accelerator plays. Driven by a combination of strong ASIC ramp as well as networking revenue upside on overall AI TAM expansion, we estimate Broadcom to grow earnings by 43% in FY27e vs peer group average of 29%. However, despite better growth expectations, it is trading at a 21x FY27e PE on our estimates, virtually in line with the peer group average of 20x (refer Exhibit 1). Hence, we believe the riskreward is attractive with multiple levers for re-rating. HSBC Equities ● Semiconductors & Equipment 24 November 2025 12

Valuation and risks We derive our revised target price of USD535.00 (previously USD400.00) by applying our FY27 target PE of 32x (from 31x) to our FY27e EPS of USD16.72 (from USD12.85). Previously, we used a target FY27e PE of 31x. Our 31x target PE was based on the 3-year historical peak PE. The revised 3-year historical peak PE is now 32x, therefore, while our rationale for the target PE remains the same, we revise our target PE in line with the revised FY27e peak PE. We believe this is justified as we believe the potential ASIC upside opportunity is still undervalued. Our FY27 earnings estimates are highest on the street − 59% higher than consensus estimates. This significant upside potential on the back of substantial ASIC momentum coupled with possible upside to AI networking can drive a re-rating of the stock and we believe it can re-rate towards its peak PE of 32x. Our revised target price of USD535.00 implies c51% upside to the current market price and we reiterate our Buy rating. We expect Broadcom can continue re-rating driven by strong ASIC momentum and potential upside in AI networking from overall AI TAM expansion.
